title: Microsoft 365 Fundamentals
subtitle: Guess the hidden Microsoft 365 terms -- spin for consonants, buy vowels

puzzles.hint: The cloud-hosted service that handles your organization's email and calendar.
puzzles.explain: Exchange Online is the cloud email component of Microsoft 365, providing each user a 50 GB mailbox on Business plans (100 GB on E3/E5). It replaces on-premises Exchange Server without requiring local hardware.

puzzles.hint: The content platform that backs every Teams channel's file storage.
puzzles.explain: SharePoint Online is the collaboration and document management platform built into Microsoft 365. Every Microsoft Teams channel automatically stores its files in a corresponding SharePoint Online document library.

puzzles.hint: Each employee gets 1 TB of personal cloud storage here; Known Folder Move redirects Desktop and Documents into it.
puzzles.explain: OneDrive for Business provides each licensed user 1 TB of personal cloud storage by default. The Known Folder Move feature automatically redirects the Desktop, Documents, and Pictures folders so files are always backed up to the cloud.

puzzles.hint: The cloud identity provider that replaced Azure Active Directory and enables single sign-on.
puzzles.explain: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is the cloud-based identity and access management service at the core of Microsoft 365. It provides single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, and Conditional Access policies across all connected applications.

puzzles.hint: Requiring more than just a password at sign-in blocks roughly 99.9 percent of account-compromise attacks.
puzzles.explain: Multi-factor authentication requires users to verify their identity through two or more methods, such as a password plus an authenticator app code. Microsoft research shows MFA blocks approximately 99.9 percent of automated credential-stuffing and phishing attacks.

puzzles.hint: Classification tags applied to documents and emails that enforce encryption and travel with the file wherever it goes.
puzzles.explain: Sensitivity labels, managed through Microsoft Purview, allow organizations to classify documents and emails as Confidential, Public, or other custom tiers. The label and its enforcement settings such as encryption and watermarking travel with the file even if it is shared outside the organization.

puzzles.hint: A security model built on three principles: verify explicitly, use least privilege, and assume breach.
puzzles.explain: Zero Trust is a security framework that assumes no user, device, or network segment is inherently trustworthy. Microsoft 365 is architected around Zero Trust principles, using continuous verification through Entra ID and Conditional Access rather than relying on a traditional perimeter.

puzzles.hint: A volume licensing commitment designed for organizations with 500 or more users, signed for a three-year term.
puzzles.explain: The Microsoft Enterprise Agreement is a volume licensing program for organizations with at least 500 users or devices, offering the deepest discounts in exchange for a three-year commitment. It provides predictable pricing and centralized license management across the entire organization.
